title: Multimodal learning separates functional motor disorders from controls
summary: A random forest combined gait, postural, neurophysiological and MRI measures in 75 people with clinically diagnosed functional motor disorders and 75 healthy controls. Repeated internal cross-validation reported AUC 0.921. MRI regions were initially derived from group differences, which may inflate performance. This does not establish differentiation from organic movement disorders, causal mechanisms or routine diagnostic utility.
organization: University of Verona; University of Salerno; University of Naples Federico II; IRCCS San Raffaele Scientific Institute

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Clinically defined cases versus healthy controls in a multicentre cross-sectional study with repeated five-fold internal validation.
evidence.unknown: Independent patient-versus-patient diagnostic validation and clinical utility remain unestablished; whole-sample imaging-region screening may introduce optimism despite later within-fold selection.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest combines behavioral, electrophysiological and imaging features to distinguish clinically established case/control labels.
